sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Commodity Trade in Whole and Skimmed Milk Powder

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (Republic of Panama; unitary national jurisdiction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic codified tradition with strong Anglo-American commercial practice influence; Private Interest Foundation statute modelled on the Liechtenstein Personen- und Gesellschaftsrecht)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama – United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA), in force since 31 October 2012, including Chapter 10 on Investment with investor-state dispute settlement
Panama – Canada Free Trade Agreement, in force since 1 April 2013, including investment protection chapter
Panama – Chile Free Trade Agreement, in force since 1 May 2008, including investment chapter
Double Taxation Agreement between Panama and the United Kingdom, in force since 2014
Double Taxation Agreement between Panama and Singapore, in force since 2011

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundation Law), as amended by Ley No. 41 de 9 de octubre de 2018; Articles 3 (creation), 4 (lawful purposes), 6 (foundation assets), 10 (minimum patrimony), 14 (Foundation Council), 18-19 (registration), and 25 (operation); general administrative procedure per Ley No. 38 de 31 de julio de 2000.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de la República de Panamá — Dirección General, Sección de Personas Jurídicas (Fundaciones de Interés Privado)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública (Public Deed) containing the Acta Fundacional / Carta Fundacional (Foundation Charter), protocolized before a Panamanian Notary Public and inscribed in the Public Registry of Panama
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum initial patrimony of B/.10,000.00 (US$10,000.00) declared in the Foundation Charter (Art. 10, Ley 25 de 1995). No statutory escrow deposit is required; the Founder must effectively assign/transfer the stated assets to the foundation estate, and the Foundation Council must evidence receipt and acceptance in the foundation's private protocol before operations commence.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL. The undersigned Foundation Council, duly appointed under the Foundation Charter, resolves: (1) to ratify the Foundation Charter and adopt the annexed Regulations; (2) to confirm the Founder's contribution of the initial patrimony of not less than US$10,000; (3) to ratify the registered office located in Panama City for all statutory purposes; (4) to appoint [Name] as Secretary, with authority to maintain books, sign commercial documents, and represent the Foundation before ministries and banks; (5) to authorize the opening of bank accounts and the filing of the MICI Aviso de Operación and MINSA sanitary permits for wholesale milk-powder trading; and (6) to fix a single-signature limit of US$50,000, above which dual signatures are required. Unanimously adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name availability search and reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Dirección de Registro de Firma y Denominaciones (online 'Registro en Línea' portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Solicitud de Búsqueda de Firma via the Public Registry's electronic portal, providing up to three proposed foundation names containing the word 'Fundación'. The Registry performs a semantic and orthographic conflict check against existing entities. Upon clearance, pay the search fee and obtain a reservation certificate valid for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Online name-search application (Solicitud de Búsqueda de Firma)
Certified copy of the Founder's passport or cédula
Three proposed names containing the word 'Fundación'
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for prior registration, file a 'recurso de reconsideración' with the Dirección General within 10 working days under Ley 38 de 2000, or simply re-file the search with three new alternative names. The name reservation is renewable for a further 30-day term.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and notarial execution of the Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Counsel drafts the Escritura Pública containing the Acta Fundacional and, if applicable, the Reglamento. The Founder, or an attorney-in-fact under a notarial power of attorney, appears before a Panamanian notary to execute the deed. The deed must state the foundation's name, registered office in Panama, minimum endowed patrimony of B/.10,000, purposes (including wholesale trading of whole and skimmed milk powder, ISIC 4633), duration, initial Foundation Council, Protector if any, beneficiary provisions, and acceptance by the Council. The notary protocolizes and delivers the testimonio for registration.
required_dossiers: Draft Foundation Charter (Acta Fundacional) and optional Regulations (Reglamento)
Identity documents of Founder, Foundation Council members, Protector (if any), and Secretary
Declaration of initial patrimony (minimum B/.10,000) with description of contributed assets
Power of attorney (poder) if the Founder acts by representative
Proof of registered office availability (lease or landlord's letter of consent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defects in the deed are cured by a supplementary 'Escritura de Aclaración' before the same notary. Substantive errors in beneficiary or Council clauses require an amendment deed approved by the Foundation Council. If the notary refuses execution due to KYC insufficiencies, provide certified source-of-funds documentation and re-execute.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing, fee payment, and statutory registration with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Dirección General, Mesa de Entrada / Registro en Línea, Sección de Personas Jurídicas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the original testimonio of the Foundation Charter with the Public Registry together with the payment of the official registry tariff (approx. US$250). The Registry examines legal compliance, internal consistency, and statutory formalities. Upon approval, the foundation is inscribed in the Legal Persons Section and assigned a registration folio (ficha), which perfects its juridical personality.
required_dossiers: Original testimonio (first notarial copy) of the Escritura Pública de la Fundación
Registry fee deposit receipt (boleta de pago)
Notarial power of attorney for filing counsel
Completed registration form referencing the application folio
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues 'prevenciones' or 'observaciones', counsel has 10 working days (extendable once) to file corrective documents under Ley 38 de 2000. A negative decision may be appealed by 'recurso de apelación' to the Dirección General, followed, if required, by a 'recurso de reconsideración' and thereafter a contentious-administrative claim before the Sala Tercera de la Corte Suprema de Justicia.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the official Registration Certificate and certified deed copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Dirección General, Oficina de Certificados
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, request a Certificado de Registro de la Fundación de Interés Privado and certified copies of the inscribed deed through the Registry's virtual certificate service. The certificate evidences the foundation's existence and legal capacity for bank account opening, licensing, and commercial contracting.
required_dossiers: Online application for certificate of registration
Payment receipt for certification fees
Registration folio (ficha) number reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains discrepancies, file a 'solicitud de corrección de certificados' with the Dirección General; typographical errors are cured by issuance of a 'fe de erratas' certified by the Registrar, usually within 3 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Foundation Council resolution, Secretary appointment, RUC registration, and Aviso de Operación filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foundation Council (internal); MICI — Ventanilla Única de Inversiones; Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the constitutive meeting of the Foundation Council to adopt the First Resolution appointing the Secretary and Protector, ratifying the registered office, and authorizing bank account opening and trade signatories. The Secretary registers the foundation for tax purposes (RUC) with DGI after the first taxable event, and files the Aviso de Operación with MICI/VUI using ISIC 4633 for wholesale dairy trade, paying the proportional annual fee (approx. US$50-200).
required_dossiers: First Foundation Council Resolution
Certificado de Registro de la Fundación
Certified copies of Charter and Regulations
RUC registration form (Solicitud de Registro Único de Contribuyente, DGI)
Aviso de Operación electronic or physical form (VUI-MICI)
Municipal certificate of use and premises title or lease
Bank KYC file (passport, references, source of funds declaration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MICI queries the Aviso de Operación, correct the economic-activity classification (ISIC 4633) and resubmit; a zoning-consistency rejection is cured by applying for a 'permiso de uso' variance before the Municipalidad. If DGI rejects the RUC application, attach the certified foundation deed and First Council Resolution, then re-file within the DGI cure period. Any MINSA inspection deficiency is remedied by an abatement plan supervised by the Dirección Nacional de Alimentos.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) — Dirección de Comercio, Ventanilla Única de Inversiones (VUI); supplementary food-safety jurisdiction of the Ministerio de Salud (MINSA), Dirección Nacional de Alimentos
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Mayorista de Productos Lácteos — ISIC 4633) and Permiso Sanitario de Funcionamiento for food storage and distribution of whole and skimmed milk powder

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental (SIAG online system)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría I — Registro Ambiental: wholesale milk-powder storage and trading without processing or transformation lines requires only initial environmental registration via SIAG; a full EIA study is not mandated. Registration is valid for 2 years and renewable.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC/particulate emissions are generated in a trading-only operation. Domestic sewage discharged to municipal networks must meet Decreto Ejecutivo No. 158 de 2018 (pH 6-9; BOD5 ≤ 300 mg/L; COD ≤ 500 mg/L; TSS ≤ 300 mg/L; oils and grease ≤ 30 mg/L). Solid waste must be handled per Ley 33 de 2018 through licensed contractors. Any refrigerated storage must use ozone-friendly refrigerants per Ley 6 de 2017, and the facility must maintain a register of refrigerant charges.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Visto Bueno del Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá (fire-prevention inspection and annual renewal covering office and warehouse premises); Municipalidad de Panamá structural and occupancy clearance for the premises (Reglamento de Diseño Estructural 2014); and MITRADEL occupational hygiene and safety registration, including the Comité de Higiene y Seguridad under Ley 7 de 1975 and implementing regulations, before any hiring of staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; operational portal: Sede Electrónica DGI (https://sede.dgi.gob.pa). Customs export controls are administered by Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Phase 1: Incorporate the Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF) at the Panamanian Public Registry and obtain the foundation charter, certificate of registration, and legal personality. Phase 2: Obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) from DGI through the Sede Electrónica portal, submitting the foundation charter, registered agent acceptance, local registered address, and identification of the foundation council or officers. Phase 3: If any Panamanian taxable commercial activity is commenced, complete the ITBMS taxpayer registration and, when applicable, register for electronic invoicing. Non-resident foreign entities without a permanent establishment in Panama are not generally required to hold a RUC unless engaged in Panama-source activities; all customs export operations must nevertheless be processed through a licensed customs broker with his/her own RUC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope: the PIF is taxed only on Panama-source income under the Panamanian territorial system. Foreign-source income from cross-border dairy commodity trading, including whole and skimmed milk powder sales to non-resident buyers, is exempt from Panamanian income tax. The PIF remains a separate legal person and, absent Panama-source income, may file an annual nil income tax return with DGI.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime and does not classify PIFs as pass-through entities by default. Available elections under Panamanian law include: (i) voluntary ITBMS registration for exporters not otherwise required to register; (ii) election to access the simplified small taxpayer regime where annual gross income does not exceed B/.36,000; (iii) election of accounting books in US dollars/Balboas at par; and (iv) election to treat certain foreign-source investments as non-taxable remittances under the territorial income tax rules. Hybrid mismatch or economic substance elections are limited by general transfer pricing and substance requirements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) - Panamanian VAT
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold exempts habitual suppliers or exporters from ITBMS registration in Panama. Any person or entity making taxable transfers of movable goods or services in Panama, or exporting goods, must register for ITBMS; under the simplified small taxpayer regime an annual gross income threshold of B/.36,000 may reduce compliance burdens, but export transactions otherwise remain zero-rated.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taxpayers issuing ITBMS invoices must use the Panamanian electronic invoicing system (Facturacion Electronica de Panama) through DGI-approved software or the DGI free portal. Invoices must be transmitted in near-real-time as structured XML/JSON files and receive a DGI authorization number; physical invoices must carry a QR code and digital stamp. Export declarations are processed through the ANA customs single-window environment, and the zero-rated export invoice must be electronically matched with the customs export declaration for fiscal clearance. Authorized electronic fiscal printers or online invoicing APIs may be required for high-volume traders, and every invoice must contain the RUC, DGI-validated series, zero-rating indicator, and product HS code for dairy goods.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The 0% ITBMS rate applies to exported movable goods and to offshore services supplied for use outside Panama. For raw milk powder dairy products, the goods must physically leave Panamanian customs territory, be destined for the account of a non-resident buyer, and be evidenced by the customs export declaration and transport documents. Sales to the Colon Free Zone may also be zero-rated if the goods are eventually re-exported, subject to the current ANA protocol. The seller must retain complete transactional documentation showing export delivery, economic substance, and foreign consideration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaracion de Mercancias de Exportacion)
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Airway Bill
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificacion de Ingreso de Divisas)
Commercial Invoice bearing the 0% ITBMS indicator
Certificate of Origin for dairy commodity shipment
Warehouse/container receipt or SISA/port exit proof
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI and ANA may jointly audit export zero-rating claims. If the required physical export documentation, transport certificates, or FX inward remittance evidence are not completed within the 180-day deadline, DGI may reverse the 0% rate and assess ITBMS at the standard 7% rate, together with statutory default interest and surcharges. Fraudulent or repeated export zero-rating claims, or the use of false export documents, also expose the taxpayer to penalties under the Codigo Fiscal and the Panamanian Customs Law, including fines up to 200% of the omited tax (B/.5,000 to B/.50,000 or more per infraction), temporary or permanent loss of the RUC, and criminal liability for trade-based money laundering, tax fraud, and smuggling.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: N/A – Panama maintains no central bank of issuance. The Republic is fully dollarized; the US Dollar (USD) is legal tender and the Panamanian Balboa (PAB) exists only as a subsidiary coin unit at a 1:1 fixed parity. Monetary and financial supervision is exercised by the Superintendency of Banks of Panama (Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá, SBP) under Decree Law 2 of 2008 and Law 23 of 2015 (AML/CFT). The Banco Nacional de Panamá (state-owned) operates the national clearing house and acts as fiscal agent. The Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) performs residual financial policy functions. There is no FX control authority because no exchange control regime exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full de jure and de facto convertibility on both current and capital accounts. Panama has no exchange controls, no surrender requirements, no prior approval for capital inflows or outflows, and no differential treatment between residents and non-residents. Profit remittance and foundation distributions to foreign beneficiaries are unrestricted and require no central bank permit; banks apply only standard KYC narrative purpose codes and FATF-compliant due diligence. The only practical friction is the absence of an own currency: all liquidity, correspondent settlement, and pricing risk is expressed in USD, so cash management is driven entirely by USD correspondent banking rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory timeline for repatriation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation on export receipts. All proceeds from the export of whole and skimmed milk powder may be held offshore or onshore in USD; in practice, SBP-regulated banks require the underlying trade documents (sales contract, commercial invoice, bill of lading, customs exit certificate) to classify proceeds as legitimate trade income and to comply with Law 23 of 2015, but the funds themselves are freely usable.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium – Limited to ancillary operations. Panama's Law 3 of 2023 (Financial Innovation Law) and SBP AML guidelines permit licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) to serve commercial clients; however, offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Airwallex, WISE-type platforms, UK/European EMI passporting) do not hold a Panamanian banking license and cannot lawfully provide principal account services to a Panama PIF without SBP authorization or a locally licensed partner bank. Legal constraint: an unlicensed offshore EMI soliciting deposits from a Panamanian foundation may violate SBP Circular SBP-G-2017-002 on advertising and the practice of banking. Recommended structure: use a Tier-1 local bank as the treasury anchor and a single licensed local EMI (or a regulated international gateway via a licensed correspondent) only for high-frequency, low-value expense flows. Feasibility rating: Medium, subject to a local agent and a written legal opinion on the EMI's licensing status.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required in practice for the founder or an appointed foundation council member at first account opening. A fully remote opening for a Private Interest Foundation is not standard at Tier-1 Panamanian banks; the prevailing SBP-sanctioned practice requires one in-person interview at the branch (or before a Panamanian notary) to verify identity, together with original PIF charter and registry certificate. Alternative: a Panamanian licensed attorney or local resident with a notarized and apostilled power of attorney may attend in person on behalf of the foundation body, but banks still reserve the right to request a video call or, in higher-risk cases, a physical meeting with the ultimate beneficial owner. For the PA_PIF structure, the founder should budget for a physical onboarding trip to Panama City.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque UBO structure – foundation beneficiaries not disclosed in public registry, frequent red flag under Law 23 of 2015 CDD rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized extract of the Foundation Charter (Acta Fundacional) and Regulations (Reglamento) naming the foundation council and benefit holders; sworn declaration of source of funds and source of wealth for the initial endowment; Panamanian attorney's legal opinion mapping the UBO chain; certificate of good standing from the Public Registry (Registro Público); current passports of founder, council members, and any protector; apostilled background reference letters from home-country banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid cross-border trading with no physical trace – high invoice counts for dairy commodities routed through multiple jurisdictions without title documents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade dossier: signed sales/purchase contracts, commercial invoices, bills of lading, packing lists, certificates of origin (e.g., EU/New Zealand/USDA export certificates), SPS health certificates, warehouse receipts, freight invoices, and customs exit/entry declarations matching invoice value and shipping dates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large round-number inbound transfers or structured deposits inconsistent with commodity trade volumes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or reviewed financial statements of the PIF; payment schedule matched to contract delivery milestones; board/council resolutions authorizing each treasury transaction; bank reference letters from the previous correspondent bank covering 12 months; narrative explanation of the commercial cycle from purchase order to final customer payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Correspondent bank exposure to high-risk or sanctioned corridors (e.g., payments routed via OFAC/UNSC-listed jurisdictions).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-by-country transaction matrix with commercial justification for each corridor; end-beneficiary declarations (KYC certificates from customers); shipping company verification of no transshipment through sanctioned ports; compliance undertaking signed by the foundation council to refrain from restricted corridors; periodic sanctions screening reports from a reputable screening provider.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for the initial foundation endowment and subsequent capital injections: (1) Priority is a direct SWIFT MT103 from the founder's home-country bank to the PIF's USD account at the Panamanian Tier-1 bank; field 70 (Remittance Information) must state 'CAPITAL APORTADO – PRIVATE INTEREST FOUNDATION – ISIC 4633 DAIRY TRADING'; field 50K must show the founder's name, and field 57A must identify the Panamanian beneficiary bank. (2) If routed through a US correspondent intermediary (e.g., Citibank NA, BNY Mellon), the MT202 COV instruction must match the MT103 mirror message. (3) Verification bundle: notarized resolution of the foundation council approving the capital contribution; source-of-funds declaration; signed subscription/donation agreement; bank remittance certificate from the sending bank; PIF Non-Profit or Private Interest Foundation registration certificate; SBP has no capital import authorization to grant, so no government permit is required. (4) For trade-related pre-finance, a commercial purpose code in field 70 is added, e.g., 'ADVANCE PAYMENT AGAINST PROFORMA INVOICE'.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Two rails: (A) SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments below USD 250,000 or for stop-gap settlements; standard execution via Banco General, Banistmo, or Global Bank with same-day USD clearing through US correspondents; narrative field must carry the invoice number and ISIC 4633 dairy commodity description. (B) Commercial documentary Letters of Credit (L/C) under UCP 600 for bulk whole and skimmed milk powder purchases exceeding USD 250,000 – issuance via MT700, amendments via MT707, and negotiation under MT740/MT752; the Panamanian bank is the issuing or confirming bank as required; the L/C must be irrevocable and payable in USD at sight or 90-day tenor. For both rails, the bank requires the trade dossier (contract, invoice, B/L, insurance, certificates) to maintain the Low-Risk Standard risk rating.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Forwards (USD/EUR, USD/GBP, USD/CNH) – freely executed with licensed Panamanian Tier-1 banks; no regulatory prior approval required
Non-Deliverable Forwards (USD/CNY and selected LatAm currencies) – permitted via the bank's international desk or a US/European counterparty, subject to board-authorized ISDA/CSA credit limits

Cross-Currency Swaps (USD/EUR, USD/CHF, USD/CNH) – permitted where the underlying milk-powder supply contract is denominated in a non-USD currency; requires foundation council resolution and standard ISDA documentation

Plain-Vanilla FX Options (EUR/USD, GBP/USD, CNH/USD) – available from the bank's treasury or via a licensed intermediary; tolerated by SBP as non-speculative hedging when documented against firm trade exposures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Franchise Tax (Impuesto Anual de la Fundación de Interés Privado) - B/.300 privilege tax that maintains the Private Interest Foundation in good standing with the Panamanian registry and tax systems
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; paid via the DGI E-Tax portal or at Banco Nacional de Panamá / Banco Caja de Ahorros
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually within the first calendar quarter (statutory window 1 January - 31 March); newly registered foundations remit the first B/.300 within 90 days of charter registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Moratory interest at 10% per annum and fines under the Código Fiscal; denial of certificates of good standing and 'Paz y Salvo'; after sustained non-payment (typically three or more consecutive years), the Registro Público may administratively dissolve and strike off the foundation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO Annual Confirmation and Attestation - Declaración de Beneficiario Final; initial beneficial-ownership return plus annual no-change/update confirmation executed by the resident agent and kept on the foundation's compliance file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUBF), filed through the licensed resident agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial declaration within 30 days of foundation registration; any change in beneficial ownership filed within 30 days of the triggering event; annual confirmation interlocked with the first-quarter franchise-tax payment and the resident agent's KYC review cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under Law 254 of 2021, late, false, or omitted UBO declarations trigger statutory fines against the foundation and its resident agent, suspension of registry rights, denial of good-standing certificates, and eventual administrative strike-off for persistent non-compliant status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Business License (Aviso de Operación) annual renewal - triggered only if the foundation maintains premises, employees, or a fixed base in Panama; pure cross-border milk-powder trading through the PIF does not normally require this license; municipal fee when applicable ranges from approximately USD 150 to USD 3,000 per annum based on declared net assets
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipalidad del distrito de ubicación (e.g., Dirección de Rentas Municipales, Municipality of Panama)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal window 1 January - 31 March, aligned with the DGI annual-tax payment calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Municipal surcharges and fines for late renewal, designation of the commercial establishment as informal, and closure of premises; inapplicable to the foundation's extraterritorial commodity-trading activity where no Panamanian establishment exists.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Private Interest Foundations under Law 25 of 1995 are exempt from statutory audit and from government filing of financial statements; no revenue-based audit threshold applies to foundation status per se. A compulsory independent audit arises only where (i) the foundation charter or Foundation Council mandates it, (ii) the foundation operates a Panamanian commercial establishment subject to territorial income tax and is classified as a large taxpayer, or (iii) the foundation is itself a regulated banking, trust, or financial institution. Cross-border trading of raw milk powder through a PIF does not trigger a statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Panama adopts IFRS as the reference framework for financial reporting (Normas de Información Financiera - NIIF/IFRS); foundations preparing statements for financing or counterparty purposes may apply IFRS, US GAAP, or the governing country's home GAAP, provided that underlying accounting records are verifiable and retained in Panama or accessible to the resident agent.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Panama does not require a standalone annual UBO renewal certificate; instead, Law 254 of 2021 mandates a permanent, currently accurate UBO register. The resident agent files the initial declaration within 30 days of registration, files any transfer or shareholding-change declaration within 30 days of the event, and performs an annual KYC review confirming the continued accuracy of the UBO register, including as applicable the notarized attestation of the Foundation Council. The annual confirmation is evidenced in the resident agent's compliance file rather than as a separate registral filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Members (Registro de Miembros de la Fundación)
Register of the Foundation Council / Directors (Registro del Consejo de la Fundación)
Minute Book of Foundation Council Resolutions (Libro de Actas y Resoluciones)
Books of Accounts and Supporting Records (Libros de Contabilidad)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 850 - USD 1,500 per annum for a Panama City registered office and licensed resident agent, including routine administration, UBO filing coordination, and annual franchise-tax settlement
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 6,500 per annum for a voluntary independent audit of the foundation's financial statements where the charter, bank, or trading counterparty requires one

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% on Panama-source net taxable income of legal entities and private interest foundations engaged in local commercial activity; territorial tax system applies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holidays. Private Interest Foundations (PIFs) under Law 25 of 1995 are exempt from Panama income tax on income generated, administered, invested, or distributed outside Panama. In-country dairy commodity trading income is taxable at 25%. Advance income tax payments of 1% of gross income (standard taxpayers) or 2% (large taxpayers) are creditable against the final 25% liability; limited investment tax credits of 3%–5% apply to qualifying fixed-asset investments in Panama.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario de Declaración de Rentas 201 (Form 201) filed electronically through the Panama DGI portal 'DIGITAX' (digitax.mef.gob.pa).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual filing due within the first 90 days after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers, due March 31 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC tax identification number and foundation registry number; legal entity identification data.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders and beneficiaries are not required to be listed; the PIF must maintain a registered Panama address and tax ID.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income from Panama-source commercial trading activity, including milk powder sale commissions, mark-ups, and logistics fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners must report only income attributed to Panama operations; foreign-source income is excluded under territorial tax principles.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income: income generated and received outside Panama by the PIF, distributions from foreign trusts, and foreign holding income under Law 25-1995.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident founders/beneficiaries may rely on the PIF's foreign-source exclusion without filing a separate Panama declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost and expenses of the dairy commodity brokering operation, including purchases from related powder producers, freight, insurance, and customs storage.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transfer pricing adjustment is required for cross-border purchases from related foreign dairy suppliers; a local file must support arm's-length prices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after allowable deductions and tax-exempt exclusions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident centers must not shift excess manufacturing or procurement profits to Panama without economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax computed at 25% on net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For PIFs with non-Panama-source income, net taxable income is zero and the 25% rate does not apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance income tax payments, dividend withholding credits, and any tax credits already paid during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder has no direct credit against Panama tax unless a DTA provides a credit mechanism.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable or refund balance after credits and advance payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No remittance abroad is permitted without a valid 'Paz y Salvo' tax certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a 10% surcharge on the tax due plus default interest of 1% per month or fraction thereof, computed from the original due date. Failure to file a nil return triggers a base fine of USD 50; repeated non-compliance can lead to suspension of the RUC, denial of export permits for dairy commodities, and notification to the Public Registry for dissolution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding on dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders; 5% on dividends paid to resident natural persons from profits already subject to corporate income tax; 10% on distributions from profits that were not subject to Panama corporate income tax. PIF capital distributions to beneficiaries are generally outside the corporate dividend regime unless classified as economic benefits from Panama-source commercial profits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama has a limited double taxation agreement network. To invoke DTA relief, the recipient must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residency (TRC) from its country of residence, submit the TRC with a completed Form 201 annex, provide evidence of beneficial ownership, and file the remittance application through the DGI 'Procedimiento de Aplicación de Tratados'. Approval is granted before the reduced rate is applied; retroactive claims are permitted in limited cases.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on royalties paid to non-residents is 20% of gross Panama-source remittances; treaty rates may reduce this to 5%–10% depending on the DTA. Interest paid to non-resident banks or lenders is subject to 5% withholding for qualified foreign bank financing and 10% for non-bank lending; a treaty can reduce interest WHT to 0%–5% subject to beneficial ownership proof.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File are required when aggregate Panama-source gross revenues exceed USD 3,000,000 in a fiscal year. A contemporaneous transfer pricing study is expected for all related-party cross-border transactions involving the purchase or sale of whole and skimmed milk powder over USD 1,000,000 per annum.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply to PIFs and corporations conducting 'relevant activities', which include distribution, agricultural commodity trading, shipping, holding, and financial services. A PIF engaged in milk powder trading must demonstrate: (a) its management and board meetings are held physically in Panama; (b) it maintains a tangible office in Panama with exclusive use; (c) it employs an adequate number of qualified full-time employees, at least one senior trader and two support staff; (d) its annual operating expenditure in Panama is proportional to the gross trading volume; and (e) it files the annual Economic Substance Declaration with the DGI. Failure to satisfy these requirements will annul the territorial tax exemption and create economic employer status in Panama.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating Panama-source commission or mark-up from milk powder sales by routing deals through a non-resident nominee intermediary while the PIF's bank account in Panama receives funding via Swift LC or TT wire.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty equal to the evaded tax plus 10% surcharge and monthly default interest at 1%; criminal prosecution under Article 853 of the Fiscal Code and Law 70 of 2019 may impose imprisonment of 2 to 5 years, a fine of up to twice the evaded tax, and confiscation of the proceeds of under-reported sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and foundation council members who knowingly sign false declarations become jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax. Courts may issue travel bans, asset freezes, and dissolution orders; a criminal conviction results in imprisonment and a permanent director disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the PIF as a pass-through instrument with no employees, no physical office in Panama, no board book, and no evidence that trading decisions are made in Panama, while claiming exemption on foreign-source milk powder trading income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Non-filing of the Economic Substance Declaration carries fines up to USD 75,000 or 1% of gross turnover, whichever is higher; repeated non-compliance results in the foundation's registration being suspended and eventually struck off the Public Registry, causing automatic loss of the territorial tax exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members cease to benefit from the limited liability shield and become personally responsible for the entire unpaid corporate tax liability, third-party debts, and employee social security obligations if the foundation continues operations without substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PIF and its bank account as a settlement vehicle for bulk milk-powder trades funded by unknown third parties or by letters of credit issued from unvetted financial institutions, without performing beneficial ownership and transaction-chain KYC under Law 23 of 2015.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering penalties range from 5 to 12 years' imprisonment for responsible individuals, plus confiscation of the full transaction amount and monetary fines of not less than USD 1 million for covered intermediaries. The PIF's banking license can be cancelled and the proceeds repatriated to the affected jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the compliance officer (CUAT) may be criminally prosecuted even if the entity itself is a foundation; personal assets can be seized under civil asset forfeiture, and professional bans extend to all regulated financial activities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Characterising Panama-source trading profits as 'capital distributions' to beneficiaries to avoid the 10% dividend withholding tax and to bypass the requirement that profits be declared and taxed at 25% in the PIF.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation as a constructive dividend: additional corporate income tax at 25% on the full distribution, a 10% dividend withholding tax payable by the PIF as withholding agent, interest from the original filing date, and a 50% penalty for deliberate concealment of taxable profit distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members act as withholding agents under Article 781 of the Fiscal Code; on failure to withhold and remit the dividend tax, they become personally liable for the full unpaid withholding amount, subject to civil restitution orders and a travel ban pending payment.
